utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a document I would have used, if not for the clock, that relates to that meeting, and I will put on the record 65 ter 06018, and just ask Mr. Lukic if he'd be willing to discuss whether it can be bar tabled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It can be bar tabled anyhow, but I take it that you want to know whether he would object against it being admitted through the bar table.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... and I wouldn't expect, Mr. President, him to have a position off the top of his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps you take your time. Mr. Traldi, in the beginning you wanted to tender from the bar table two documents: One which was not objected to; the other one was 16582, 65 ter number. Is that report anywhere footnoted in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. Then, Mr. Lukic, the only objection you raised is that these are various reports. They all seem to be signed. They all seem to refer at least in one way or another to how people were moved from municipalities to finally to Manjaca camp. This document now in your cross-examination you, of course, challenged some of the findings here. Do you still against a footnoted material to be in evidence just because you have issues with it and there are several signatures? These are several documents. They all deal more or less with similar things, although in different municipalities or with prisoners ending up in Manjaca. Which was a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To be honest with you I received it in time from Mr. Traldi, but I was doing on some other things. So I just raised the first objection I could see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But to be more specific, maybe I really need more time. It might be that I will not object, but I have to go through the document [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... let's then wait for that. So you are now considering your position rather than having objected to admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll MFI it. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2900, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, if I might beg the interpreters' indulgence for two or three more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although it's not only the interpreters. There are other matters as well. We can't finish very late. I have commitments elsewhere. So if you would try to keep it short, with the assistance of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 07055. And that will be the last document I use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Say the number again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My notes appear to be in error -- no. We have the right document on the left and not on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Under point 4, this document is a 1st Krajina Corps report to the Main Staff dated 16 December. In point 4, it reports: "Pursuant to your order, we are, with some difficulty, closing down Manjaca camp." What do you take from this?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the 1st Krajina Corps is responding to a tasking it received to close the camp down which it is carrying out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 65 ter 7055 receives number P2901, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2901 is admitted. 2901 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, earlier today you mentioned that when the camp was reopened in 1993, Colonel Popovic had been promoted and was put back in charge. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: EWAN McGREGOR BROWN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, actually. I think that despite all the paperwork in relation to abiding by Geneva Conventions, it speaks volumes that the documents that they had knew what was happening in Manjaca and the same commander was appointed and promoted, and it high lights that actually behind this the Bosnian Serb, the VRS, did not care and did not have any intentions of taking -- making anyone accountable for these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Have the questions in re-direct triggered any need for further question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that. But I would -- I would defend before the interpreters that if you would need one or two more minutes and -- if it's a -- if it's an important and relevant issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... many issues, but we will try to clarify them with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that's your -- I would have assisted you but that's where we are. Then, first of all, Mr. Brown, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to this courtroom and for having answered all the questions - I can say the many questions - that were put to you by the parties and the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. You are excused and may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. And I do apologise for some of the length of the questions. Sometimes context is not very easy. And I also would like to thank the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're apologising for the length of the questions, I think Mr. Lukic would really appreciate that, but I take it that also includes the length of your answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender at this point exhibit MFI numbers P2859 through 2863 which are his reports, statements, and errata sheets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would not mind, we leave that until next week to decide on it and to see whether there are any additional objections by the Defence. So that's the first thing on the agenda of Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I will submit a list of associated exhibits for tendering at that time as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we can deal with them in one -- one -- in one -- in one step. Nothing else to be raised. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume Monday, the 25th of November, at 9.30 in the morning. Mr. Registrar, would that still be in this Courtroom III or -- still in Courtroom III. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of November, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
